hero.headline: We started this to do things differently.
hero.subtext: We've lived the challenges of growing a business with disconnected systems, limited resources, and solutions that didn't quite fit. We've also worked with consultants who brought rigid frameworks, pushed software, and overlooked how the business actually runs day to day. That's not how we work. We partner with businesses to build practical, flexible systems that support how they actually operate; without unnecessary complexity, cost, or rigid frameworks. We believe the best work happens through real partnership; which is why we choose to work with clients who value collaboration, transparency, and doing things the right way.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.text: To make operations easy; not in a naive way, but in the way that comes from having the right systems, the right data, and the right processes working together. We give growing teams the connected infrastructure they need to grow without the chaos, without bloated consulting fees, and without cookie-cutter solutions that don't fit.

gamesPrivacy.title: Privacy policy, Awesoon games
gamesPrivacy.updated: Last updated 10 November 2026. Version 2, for game versions 1.1.0 and later. Earlier versions show no ads and collect nothing.
gamesPrivacy.lead: Our games run on your device. The only data that leaves it is what the advertising software collects, and you make the choices.
gamesPrivacy.appliesTo: Applies to all ten Awesoon games: Stack Snap, Loop Weaver, Tidy Tiles, Idle Bakery Empire, Quick Trivia Blitz, Dodge Rush, Word Chain Dash, Color Match Frenzy, Knot Untangle and Bounce Blitz. The games are published by Awesoon Technologies Inc., a company in British Columbia, Canada.

p: There is no account, no sign-in and no server of ours. Your progress, scores, statistics, settings and the answer to the age question are stored on the device itself. They are never sent to us or to anyone else. The games collect nothing, and this website uses analytics only with your consent.

The first time you open a game, it asks your birth month and year. Nothing is filled in beforehand. The answer stays on your device, is never sent to us or to Google, and cannot be changed by going back. It decides which ads you see. On iPhone and iPad, if Apple tells the game your device belongs to someone under 13, that overrides your answer. On Android, the game follows your answer alone.

sections.h: Advertising and what Google AdMob collects
p: The games show ads served by Google AdMob. Its software is built into each game. It may collect your advertising ID, your IP address and device data such as the device model, system version, language and how you interact with ads. Google uses this to show and measure ads and to prevent fraud. The data goes to Google, under Google's own privacy policy at policies.google.com/privacy. We do not receive it. We see only aggregate earnings reports.

sections.h: Your choices if you are 13 or over
p: On iPhone and iPad, the game asks for your permission to track you. If you decline, you still see ads, but they are not personalised. In the European Economic Area, the UK and Switzerland, Google's consent form runs before any personalised ads, and a row in the game's Settings reopens it so you can change your answer. On Android you can reset or delete your advertising ID in your device's settings.

Our games are for players of all ages. We ask your birth month and year once, on your device only. If you are under 13, ads are limited to a child-safe setting and no advertising ID is used. Players under 13 still play the whole game. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. A parent or guardian who has a question can write to us at the address below.

Progress and settings stay on your device until you delete the game or reset it. Emails you send us are deleted 12 months after our last reply. Ad data is held by Google under its own policies. We hold none of it. Several games also have a reset option in Settings that clears progress without deleting the app.

We hold almost nothing about players: only the emails you send us. If you live in the European Economic Area or the UK (GDPR and UK GDPR), in Brazil (LGPD) or in California (CCPA and CPRA), you can ask us for a copy of what we hold about you, ask us to correct or delete it, object to or restrict how it is used, and withdraw consent you gave. In the EEA, the UK and Brazil you can also complain to your data protection authority. Where we rely on consent, which is the case for personalised ads, you can withdraw it at any time using the choices above.

We do not sell personal information. Ad data that Google collects through its software can count as sharing for advertising under California law. If you are 13 or over you can opt out by declining the tracking prompt or the consent form, and under 13 no advertising ID is used. We do not treat you differently for using these rights. Write to us to use any of them. We reply within the time your local law sets: one month under GDPR and UK GDPR, 15 days under Brazilian law and 45 days under California law. Requests about ad data held by Google go to Google as well.
If this policy changes, the new version is posted on this page with a new date above, before the game version that needs it is released. Earlier versions stay posted, and version 1 is linked below.

platforms.title: The platforms we actually know
platforms.text: We are vendor-neutral. We pick what fits your operations, not what pays a commission.

fit.netsuite: Cloud-first ERP for multi-entity businesses with strong finance and reporting needs. A strong pick for companies that outgrew QuickBooks.
fit.odoo: All-in-one suite: ERP, CRM, inventory, ecommerce. Ideal when you want one connected stack without per-module lock-in.
fit.epicor: Deep manufacturing and distribution ERP with complex production workflows, BOMs and shop floor control.
fit.sap: SAP-grade financial controls and audit trails without the overhead of a full S/4HANA deployment.
fit.salesforce: Sales-led teams with complex pipelines, custom objects and high forecast accuracy needs.
fit.hubspot: Marketing-driven teams that want fast adoption, inbound workflows and tight sales and marketing alignment.
fit.zoho: A full CRM suite without enterprise pricing. Good for lean teams that need breadth without complexity.
fit.pipedrive: Simple pipeline visibility for small sales teams that want speed over configuration depth.
fit.shopify: Our default for B2C and mid-complexity B2B. Fast to launch, easy to run, huge app ecosystem.
fit.magento: Complex catalogs, tiered B2B pricing and deep customization, for when Shopify is not enough.
fit.woocommerce: Content-driven stores on WordPress with full ownership of hosting and plugins.
fit.bigcommerce: Hybrid SaaS and headless, with stronger native B2B features than Shopify Basic.
fit.celigo: Integration platform built for NetSuite and ecommerce, with connectors for the stack we see most.
fit.boomi: Enterprise integration with strong data transformation, governance and error handling.
fit.zapier: Fast app-to-app automation when speed matters more than depth. Good for non-critical workflows.
fit.make: Visual workflow builder with deeper logic than Zapier, for complex multi-step flows.
fit.openai: GPT-based copilots, reasoning and document intelligence.
fit.anthropic: Claude for long-context analysis, production agents and safer tool use.
fit.langchain: Framework for building RAG pipelines, agents and multi-step AI workflows.
fit.postgresql: Our default database, with pgvector for AI embeddings and no separate vector store.
